<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Business and economy
*[[Economy of Brazil]]
**[[Pedro Parente]], the head of [[Brazil Petrobras]], resigns among protests related to [[diesel fuel]] prices. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-44336781 (BBC)]
*[[Visa Inc.|Visa]] card payments are disrupted throughout [[Europe]] due to a network failure. The disruption results in large queues at supermarkets and petrol stations. [[Mastercard]] and [[American Express]] say they were not affected. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-44335804 (BBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Twelve people are killed and 15 injured after a bus fell 200 meters down a road in [[Palpa District]], [[Nepal]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-06/01/c_137223458.htm (Xinhua)]

;Health and environment 
*The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] reports that five people have died and 197 have been hospitalized in the [[United States]], in the largest incidence of [[E. coli]] since the [[2006 North American E. coli outbreak]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-44335702 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[Shangri-La Dialogue]]
**The annual three-day regional security forum begins in [[Singapore]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/politics/busy-day-of-bilateral-meetings-ahead-of-shangri-la-dialogue (''The Straits Times'')] 
*[[2018 North Korea–United States summit]], [[North Korea–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] officially announces that the summit will resume as scheduled following a [[White House]] meeting with [[North Korea]]n general [[Kim Yong-chol]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-44339003 (BBC)]
*[[Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh]]
**The government of [[Myanmar]] announces that it has reached a [[repatriation]] agreement with the [[United Nations]] regarding [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]] refugees in [[Bangladesh]], saying it will assure that refugees "can return voluntarily in safety and dignity." Members of the [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees|UNHCR]] and the [[United Nations Development Programme|UNDP]] will be allowed to work in [[Rakhine State]] to monitor the process. [https://www.theguardian.com/global/2018/jun/01/myanmar-and-un-announce-deal-for-safe-return-of-rohingya (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Human rights in Burkina Faso]]
**[[Burkina Faso]]'s [[National Assembly of Burkina Faso|National Assembly]] votes to abolish the [[Capital punishment|death penalty]]. [https://www.news24.com/Africa/News/burkina-faso-abolishes-death-penalty-in-new-penal-code-20180601 (News24)]
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**Federal prosecutors in [[Germany]] apply in a [[Schleswig-Holstein]] court for the extradition of [[Carles Puigdemont]] to [[Spain]], arguing that the [[treason]] charges are valid according to [[Law of Germany|German law]], because, according to the prosecutors, "the violence in Catalonia on election day can be attributed to the wanted individual". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/06/german-prosecutors-apply-puigdemont-extradition-180601115207294.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Crime in Canada]]
**Former [[Taliban]] hostage Joshua Boyle is released from jail with strict bail conditions, including an electronic tracking bracelet. [https://globalnews.ca/news/4248364/joshua-boyle-bail-conditions/ (Global News)]
*A [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] report presented to the [[United States Congress]] estimates at 499 the number of [[Civilian casualties|civilian deaths]] in US military actions during the year 2017, with more than 450 reports remaining to be assessed. The casualties occurred in [[Syria]], [[Iraq]], [[Afghanistan]] and [[Yemen]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/06/01/politics/us-military-report-civilian-deaths/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Crime in Colorado]]
**An [[Uber]] driver in [[Denver]], [[Colorado]], [[United States]], fatally shoots a passenger after a conflict on the [[Interstate 25]] highway. A portion of the highway is placed on lockdown following the incident. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/crime/uber-driver-shoots-passenger-dead-on-denver-highway-police-say/ar-AAy6LgO?ocid=spartanntp (NBC News via MSN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2018 vote of no confidence in the government of Mariano Rajoy]], [[Gürtel case]]
**The [[Rajoy II Government|Government]] of [[Mariano Rajoy]] is ousted after a [[motion of no confidence]] passes 180–169. [[Pedro Sánchez]] of the [[Spanish Socialist Workers' Party|Socialist Workers' Party]] is sworn in as the new [[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]]. This is the first time in [[History of Spain|Spanish history]] that a vote of no confidence has resulted in a change of government. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-44327573 (BBC)]
*[[2018 Italian government formation]]
**[[Giuseppe Conte]] is sworn in as the new [[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] of [[Italy]] at the head of a [[Government of Change|populist coalition]], formed by the [[Five Star Movement]] and the [[Lega Nord|Northern League]]. Conte had previously given up on trying to form a government after [[President of Italy|President]] [[Sergio Mattarella]] had vetoed Conte's original choice for [[Italian Minister of Economy and Finances|Minister of Finance]], but a different candidate was agreed to yesterday. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-44322429 (BBC)]
